clusters.name: Breathing mechanics
clusters.fact: Breathing changes chest volume and pressure to move air: quiet inhalation uses muscle contraction, while quiet exhalation mostly follows elastic recoil.

diaphragm.text: The dome-shaped muscle beneath the lungs; when it contracts and moves downward, the chest cavity expands and air is drawn in.

inhalation.text: Breathing in: expansion of the chest lowers pressure inside the lungs, drawing air through the airways.

exhalation.text: Breathing out: at rest, the breathing muscles relax and elastic recoil pushes air from the lungs.

intercostal muscles.text: Muscles between the ribs that help expand or compress the chest during breathing.

clusters.name: Alveolar gas exchange
clusters.fact: Across the thin alveolar-capillary membrane, oxygen diffuses into blood while carbon dioxide diffuses into the alveoli.

alveoli.text: Millions of tiny air sacs that provide a large, thin surface where the lungs exchange gases with blood.

pulmonary capillaries.text: Microscopic blood vessels wrapped around the alveoli, bringing blood close enough for oxygen and carbon dioxide to cross.

diffusion.text: The passive movement of gases down a partial-pressure gradient, requiring no direct expenditure of cellular energy.

partial pressure.text: The pressure contributed by one gas in a mixture; differences in oxygen and carbon dioxide partial pressure drive their diffusion.

clusters.name: Blood gas transport
clusters.fact: Most oxygen travels bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells, while most carbon dioxide is converted to bicarbonate and carried in plasma.

hemoglobin.text: The iron-containing protein in red blood cells that binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it to tissues.

red blood cells.text: Flexible blood cells packed with hemoglobin, specialized to carry respiratory gases through the circulation.

oxygen saturation.text: The percentage of hemoglobin binding sites occupied by oxygen; a pulse oximeter estimates this value noninvasively.

bicarbonate.text: The ion that carries most carbon dioxide through blood plasma after carbon dioxide is converted inside red blood cells.

bridges.fact: Ventilation bridges mechanics and exchange: each breath refreshes alveolar air, preserving the pressure gradients that let oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse.

info.text: The bulk movement of air into and out of the lungs, continually refreshing the gases available at the alveoli.

bridges.fact: Oxygen bridges exchange and transport: it diffuses from alveoli into pulmonary capillaries, then binds hemoglobin for delivery to tissues.

info.text: A respiratory gas taken up in the lungs and carried mainly by hemoglobin to support aerobic metabolism throughout the body.
